An earthquake on {StarSystem} IV has unearthed a hidden installation, lost for centuries - and still somehow populated.

“They say,” the ambassador murmurs, “that they are all that remains of {PlayerHouse}.”
Accessible from any House member's action menu.

You can make contact with the subterranean community in {StarSystem}: the "last survivors of {PlayerHouse}."

<helptext>Negotiate with Lost Installation</helptext> is available from the action list of any adult House Member who does not have an assignment.
Must not already have an assignment: the facility will take too long to travel to
This character just returned from the lost installation, and doesn't have time to go again this turn
{TargetCharacter} creeps into the tunnels, seeking the subterranean society

In a cavern beyond, ten warriors kneel before a rock pillar. Each warrior is carving {PlayerHouse}’s symbol into the flesh of their forearm.

“For {PlayerHouse}!” their leader chants. “For our blood! Our ancestors!” Suddenly, he spots {TargetCharacter}. “We have a visitor!” he grins. “But we only permit guests who prove their worth!” 

The crowd level their hewing-spears.
The leader quizzes {him(TargetCharacter)} on obscure House history, but {d(TargetCharacter)} persuades the warriors of {his(TargetCharacter)} lineage.
But the crowd is not convinced.
“Bless this bout, those of {PlayerHouse} who came before me!” {he(TargetCharacter)} roars, diving into the fray.

{He(TargetCharacter)} parries each spear-thrust, striking quickly.

“Hold!” the leader cries, as the fourth combatant falls. “You’ve proven your worth, {man(TargetCharacter)} of {PlayerHouse}.”
But their numbers are too great; {dis(TargetCharacter)} overwhelmed.
“Our cousins are returned!” the leader cries

He explains his people were sent on a {PlayerHouse} mission of conquest in the 2300s. But while holding this installation, an earthquake cut them off from the surface.

“Since then we have lived off the air recyclers and hydroponics,” he growls, “waiting for the earth to spew us out again. We’re eager to return to {HomeSystem}.”

{Assignee} secures them passage on a slow freighter. But the leader insists on joining {him(Assignee)} on {his(Assignee)} return trip, “to see you still honor the House codes.”
Weeks later, the leader bursts into a council meeting

“I was sworn into {PlayerHouse} at the age of ten! Who are you to deny my bloodright?”

Your councillors eye the dead guards at his feet. You have little choice, it seems.
Feels threatened by Dark Age cousins
The 2300s, you recall, were a Dark Age: no doubt the source of {d_s(NewCharacter)} ruthless honour-code. {His(NewCharacter)} morality seems barbaric.
The leader of a group of refugees from {Context}, stranded for centuries.
{Character} is the result of centuries of limited genetic selection within a closed community.
The Dark Age settlers arrive in {StarSystem} to a reunion feast

{PlayerHouse} look on, dumbfounded, as their distant cousins toss knives at each other and partake in ribald drinking games. Is this how their ancestors behaved?

The next morning, through splitting hangovers, the cultural work begins. The Dark Age workers are integrated into your labour-pool, their upper ranks retrained as officers. They bristle under their new, “pale-blooded” way of life.
Your House's distant forebears, cut off from civilisation for centuries, now reside here - causing cultural friction.

“For blood and seizure!” the warriors cry. They leap at the chance to join the fleet and “blood the stars.” Their ruthless attitude and unconventional tactics may prove useful.
Dark Age warriors in {House} are eager to do battle.
Your Dark Age cousins are restless in peacetime

These single-minded warriors have trained for bloodshed all their lives, even if it was within a subterranean prison. Without a war to fight - a chance to finally “blood the stars” - they lack purpose.
I’m preparing for war as we speak

{Character}’s death triggers a wave of mourning among the Dark Age community

{His(Character)} cousin {NewCharacter} rises.

“I cannot replace such a warrior, but I vow to lead this band, and guide {PlayerHouse} in the ways of blood and seizure!”

Your Dark Age cousins are eager to continue their conquest
“We held {ClaimSystem} centuries before {CurrentHouse}. It is ours to claim by force!”

During a staff meeting, {he(Leader)} suddenly kicks back {his(Leader)} stool, leaps onto the desk and draws {his(Leader)} sidearm.

“I am sickened by what this House has become,” {he(Leader)} growls. “Only my guidance can restore the ways of blood and seizure. Name me heir, and accept the old ways.”

{D(Heir)} is up like lightning. “Over my dead body!” {he(Heir)} spits.

{Leader} sniffs. “That is not the threat you think it is.”
I name you heir; guide us in the old ways
{He(Leader)} slits {his(Leader)} palm and swears a blood pact to protect {PlayerHouse}. When it’s over, the Dark Age warriors cheer, sweeping {him(Leader)} to the banquet hall.
{KindestHouseMember} shudders. “This sends a message. About what {PlayerHouse} is.”
Inspired by a legacy of ruthless conquest, {House} have become feared conquererors.

“We are the true {PlayerHouse},” {Leader} hisses, “and we will resume our conquest!” 

Betrayed from within, your security forces are in disarray. The warriors pillage their way to the spaceport, seize {PlayerHouse}’s fleet and take to the stars.
{KindestHouseMember} sighs. “It’s a shame. But our House is not what it was - which is a good thing.”

But {his(Leader)} warriors turn their weapons on {him(Leader)}. “You no longer speak for us! We’ve found a home here - a new way of being {PlayerHouse}.”

“Traitors!” {he(Leader)} cries. The melee is quick, and brutal. {He(Leader)} dies bravely.
{KindestHouseMember} sighs. “It’s a shame. But our House is not what it was - which is a good thing.”
Dark Age warriors are swelling {PlayerHouse}'s ranks

Now that you’ve embraced {PlayerHouse}’s conquering heritage, Dark Age warriors are eager to contribute, taking fleet service and encouraging recruitment.

Two high-ranking cousins have even insisted on joining the inner House.
